proposed_rules.trigger: A [3x1] zone at the very top of the page (y=0, ~80px tall, sized like the nav bar) contains raw JS source text instead of nav links.
proposed_rules.decision: Exclude the JS text from the block/content inventory; flag for Phase 2 DOM-based nav re-extraction rather than concluding the page has no nav.
proposed_rules.rationale: The nav-sized bounding box containing JS source indicates the visual capture ran before script execution replaced placeholder markup with real nav; distinct from the confirmed leaked-css-text-node rule which covers CSS leaks.

proposed_rules.trigger: A bottom-of-page zone starting with 'The best no-code platform for...' followed by a '| |' link row, identical across pages.
proposed_rules.decision: Model as a global site-wide footer fragment excluded from each page's per-page block inventory, same treatment as nav.
proposed_rules.rationale: Identical text/markup at the same position on every page is footer chrome, not page content. Alternatives rejected: authoring it as a per-page CTA/newsletter block (rejected because it never varies by page).

provenance.evidence: C162 rc3 'The best no-code platform for...' + '| |'

proposed_rules.trigger: A stray [region] node appears as a top-level sibling near the end of the tree, at coordinates overlapping an already-captured FAQ accordion answer, duplicating its text.
proposed_rules.decision: Treat as a duplicate of the corresponding accordion answer already modeled inside the FAQ block; do not count as extra content.
proposed_rules.rationale: Absolutely-positioned answer panels get promoted out of their DOM parent by the capture tool and re-appear as an extra top-level node; this is a capture artifact, not additional content.

provenance.evidence: C162 rc4 [region] 934x124 duplicates an answer already inside rc2c11
